title: Chapter 560
paragraphs: Chapter 560
147th Episode. The King of the Black Sea, Gliyak (4)
Gliyak.
The King of the Black Sea, who existed in the form of a white stone, was clearly awakened by using Dante as a vessel, judging from the circumstances.
As the bastard said, his body was very likely to have already disappeared, but perhaps some of his consciousness might still remain.
Of course, it could be a misconception.
His desperate hope for his friend to be alive might be clouding his judgment.
But Jin couldn't understand why Gliyak hesitated for a moment when his giant sword of chaos struck him.
'Did he just wake up and he's not in perfect condition?'
Jin was aware that Gliyak was not in good shape. Although this was his first time seeing him, it was because there were defects all over his twisted body.
Above all, Gliyak was mistaking Jin for 'Solderet'.
'If he's confused to the point of mistaking me for Solderet, whom he knows well and despises intensely, it means there's a problem with his sanity.'
The fact gave him chills. Despite not being fully awake, he was overwhelming everyone on the battlefield.
Kwooooong...!
Rashid, dyed in ash, struck Gliyak's upper body. With a strike filled with his whole spirit, Ron was able to break a few of his swords and spears for the first time since Gliyak awakened.
The broken weapons poured down like a landslide, pounding the ground. Ron dashed through the broken weapons once more, riding a gust of sword wind, and thrust Rashid towards Gliyak's face.
Again, hundreds of arms blocked his way, and this time a repulsion occurred instead of attraction, pushing him back.
Still, Ron was able to leave a long, deep cut on his face.
It wasn't without cost. Ron was also pierced all over his body by thorns that sprang out of nowhere from Gliyak's face.
Jin and the Black Knights leapt at the same time to protect Ron, who was momentarily defenseless.
The thorns that had pierced his body totaled sixteen, and crimson blood gushed out all over his body, but fortunately, there were no very deep wounds.
However, the problem was the fact that Ron was injured by the thorns Gliyak reflexively emitted.
The speed of the thorns that Jin and the Black Knights felt was definitely not a level that a knight like Ron couldn't dodge or fend off.
He's physically at his limit.
From the start of the second battle, he wasn't in a normal state, so it wouldn't be strange if Ron collapsed at any time.
"Sir Ron, are you okay!"
For a moment, Jin saw Ron's eyes cloud over. He could smell the ash-like scent that was peculiar to those approaching death from him.
"I'm... fine."
Jin and the Black Knights looked around left and right and behind.
Talaris was still holding his left side, and the support from Runcandel and Zipple was still only from a distance.
He's not fully sane, and he's pouring almost all of his attacks on Jin's side.
Gliyak was not completely disregarding the rear. He was continuously causing chaos to explode towards the outside, preventing Runcandel and Zipple from approaching.
More than 90% of the energy of chaos was poured into blocking the reinforcements.
Hence, what Jin's party was enduring was mostly his pure physical attacks.
Ron stood up, using his sword to push off the ground. In the process, he suddenly realized that the ground was turning unusually black. Jin and the Black Knights also noticed the same phenomenon.
"The ground, this is...."
It was not darkened by the heat or saturation of the battle.
'It's similar to... the Black Sea.'
The land named after the black sea, the Black Sea.

Star, who had participated in the expedition of the Shilong for a long time after becoming a Black Knight, had directly experienced this phenomenon in the past. The phenomenon where the land becomes 'blackened.'
Jin also encountered the same content when he heard about Ozdoc from Picon Minche.
-[As the Black Sea rapidly expanded, Ozdoc was covered in the land filled with the poison of the Black Sea. It's like being buried alive while trying to sleep.]
The land where the Black Imperial City was located was being blackened due to Gliyak's energy. The land where humans can't... survive.
Crunch!
Ron clenched his fist, grabbing a handful of the ground. Instead of black soil, solid chaos crystals filled his hand.
"How far are you going to trample on my land...."
The chaos crystals in Ron's hand disintegrated into particles and scattered somewhere. Jin couldn't say anything to him.
Perhaps all the tragedies that occurred in the Black Imperial City stemmed from his own return, and a terrible sense of guilt was stuck in his heart like rancid oil.
Zipple had made the magic stone before he returned, the royal family always sought an opportunity to push out Hairan, and the White Stone was always there.
The battle of the Black Imperial City was an event that was bound to happen regardless of Jin's return. Rather, it may be moving towards a better result because Jin is here now.
But no one could tell Jin that this wasn't his fault. Jin himself couldn't think that way, and the sorrow of the giant in front of him was unbearably poignant.
He just had to fight with all his might. As always, it was the best Jin could do.
The oppressive force pressing down on Gliyak was fading.
Tess's energy had run out. Gliyak paused for a moment as if shocked by the gash on his face, but soon started swinging hundreds of swords and spears again.
And Ron faltered.
His staggering two legs were infinitely unstable, and so now it was almost to the point where Jin and the Black Knights were protecting Ron.
After the blackening began, Gliyak's energy was insanely rapidly painting the ground black.
Jin was also getting tired. Star and the Black Knights were better off since the battle wasn't that long, but they were rapidly losing stamina due to enduring the chaos and filling in Ron's gap.
What was more painful was the fact that as the blackening progressed, Gliyak's distorted appearance was becoming more stable.
His attacks became more and more fierce over time, and his energy broadened. The breakthroughs of Runcandel and Zipple had to slow down.
Crack, clang!
Ultimately, the one dark sword that Jin and the Black Knights missed struck Ron. He barely managed to deflect it, but his body weakly floated before slamming into the ground.
He had already surpassed his limits several times. From the moment he awoke from a long coma to this moment, Ron had continuously performed miracles.
But he had reached his end…
"Sir Ron!"
"The 12th Knight!"
Jin and Star shouted simultaneously. Jin reflexively threw himself to save Ron, and Star thought that decision was wrong.
Star was right. By losing their focus on protecting Ron, they would only provide an opportunity for Gliyak.
Jin thought that Gliyak would naturally target him as he rashly stepped forward. He believed that, with Star and the Black Knights there, even if he got hurt, he could save Ron.
But as the ground turned into a Black Sea, Gliyak was regaining his rationality. He decided it was best to kill Ron first when the opportunity presented itself.
Moreover, Gliyak's spear was faster than Jin. The giant black spear was falling like a lightning bolt towards Ron.
'Damn it, damn it, damn it!'
Jin gathered his energy and launched a light-speed stab. Blood spurted from his mouth and nose, and his ultimate move...
Missed the spear by a hair's breadth. In that split second, Jin cursed himself for failing to intercept such a massive spear.
Ron didn't have the strength left to deflect the spear. The moment the spear was about to strike Ron was imprinted in Jin's vision like a slow-motion scene.
Then, once again, Jin saw...
Gliyak hesitating. The spear had stopped just before it was about to pin Ron down.
'This...'
Though it was a brief moment of just about one second, it was enough time for Jin to throw himself again and push Ron out of the way.
"Arrgh!"

Jin took the spear instead of Ron and let out a scream. He felt as if his bones and organs were about to burst due to the backflow reaction, but the relief of saving Ron made the pain feel almost gratifying.
The following attacks from Star and the Black Knights were repelled. They too were now realizing that something was off with Gliyak. However, they didn't think about Dante.
On the other hand, Ron, even as his consciousness was fading and his vision was turning pitch black, recognized it clearly.
Dante... Dante, my grandson, hey...
How can you be there, how...
His cloudy eyes.
When Jin asked if he was okay earlier, the reason Ron responded in a mumble wasn't just because he was tired.
The moment the fourteen thorns sprouted from Gliyak's face and pierced his body, he, like Jin, wondered if some part of Dante's consciousness might still exist somewhere in that monster.
Now he was certain.
"I can feel it, Jin. Inside it, my grandson, Dante is there."
[Stubborn...]
Ron's vision went dark.
He had lost his sight.
"Yes, son, it's grandpa."
The flame of his physical body was fading, and all that remained for Ron was his blind will of love for his grandson.
That was what kept him talking in a weak voice, even though his body was nearly senseless.
"Sir Ron, Dante is inside that creature. So you must hold onto your consciousness!"
"Dante... I will save you..."
Crash, creak-!
While Ron was murmuring, Gliyak was swinging his sword again. Jin and the Black Knights were fighting back, but if they missed just one more attack, Ron would be torn to shreds without a trace.
Unlike Jin, the Black Knights now believed that protecting Ron was meaningless. Unless they used Numereus's Tears, regeneration seemed impossible.
But Jin stubbornly protected Ron.
"Knight of the 12th Order, we have to give up. It's too much now."
"No, we must save him, Sir Star."
"Are you saying you really don't understand that acting on emotion won't improve the situation!"
That was not correct.
In fact, Jin was making his decision almost without emotion.
The reason he wanted to save Ron was clear.
Kelliark Jifl.
Because he was aware that the person who pushed Hairan into such a cruel fate was soon going to arrive.
'He... will definitely save Sir Ron.'
With the power of the Devil Stone.
Whether it should really be described as 'saving', he wasn't sure, but one thing was certain. Using the power of the Devil Stone, Ron could fight again, even though...
Even though it was an act that far exceeded reasonable limits.
Star, reading Jin's expression, realized his intentions late, and felt a chill run down his back.
If it was a matter of giving in to sorrow, Jin would have given up on Ron.
Surely, letting him rest now would be better than forcing him to fight again relying on the damned thing called the Devil Stone.
But what Ron wanted was not rest.
What he wanted was to fight until he could recover something of Dante's traces, something that constituted Dante, if anything was left on this desolate battlefield.
He didn't need to shy away from any terrible or cruel means to do it.
Especially since he knew that his grandson still existed somewhere in that monster.

"Kelliark Jifl will take action on Sir Ron, and Sir Ron will fight. More than anything, this fight absolutely needs Sir Ron. Since the Lord is not here. Black Knight Captain, do you really think I am ruining things because of my emotions!"
Barely suppressing his bleak feelings, Jin spoke as if spitting out the words.
